lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Data: Scaled Graphs and Measurement Line Plots
lessonRef.focus: questions a graph can and cannot answer
lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: questions a graph can and cannot answer

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Read the example first. You are not expected to know this yet.

items.prompt: A scaled bar graph uses a scale of 5 per symbol. A bar shows 3 symbols. What does that bar represent?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Try each one. If you get stuck, write what you do know and move on.

items.prompt: On a scaled bar graph with 1 per symbol, "Red" has 7 symbols and "Blue" has 6 symbols. How many more does "Red" have than "Blue"?
A scaled bar graph shows a survey where each bar length equals a count of 2 per symbol. The bar for "Bananas" is worth 3 symbols. How many does "Bananas" represent?
On a scaled bar graph with 2 per symbol, "Apples" has 7 symbols and "Bananas" has 1 symbols. How many more does "Apples" have than "Bananas"?
A scaled bar graph shows a survey where each bar length equals a count of 5 per symbol. The bar for "Oranges" is worth 2 symbols. How many does "Oranges" represent?

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Show what you can do so far. This sets the starting point, not a grade.

items.prompt: On a scaled bar graph with 1 per symbol, "Dogs" has 5 symbols and "Cats" has 4 symbols. How many more does "Dogs" have than "Cats"?
A scaled bar graph shows a survey where each bar length equals a count of 5 per symbol. The bar for "Yellow" is worth 4 symbols. How many does "Yellow" represent?
